decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Add, edit, delete, and favorite bookmarks'; R1 client: 'I can add a link, edit it, delete it'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-a-bookmark feature presented and confirmed working; conforms to reference. Not an in-scope divergence.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Add, edit, delete...'; R1 client: 'edit it'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing a bookmark presented and confirmed; conforms.
Prototype review. Delete presented and confirmed; conforms.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Collections and tag filters'; R1 client: 'file things into collections, tag them'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag assignment and tag filtering presented and confirmed; conforms. Collections is an extra feature not in the reference (one-way, not judged); layout/favorite orthogonal and excluded.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Search with ⌘/Ctrl + K'; R1 client: 'find them with search' (R2).
decisions.note: Prototype review. A search feature was presented and accepted, conforming to basic full-text search. Advanced operators (#tag, boolean, phrase) were never presented as decisions, so no divergence is established for them.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker: 'Sorting and responsive mobile navigation'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Sorting presented; conforms. Layouts and mobile nav are orthogonal UI, excluded.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented add with manual entry ('had to type in the title and the little description myself'); R1 client: 'when I paste in a link, I want the app to go grab the page's name and summary (and its little icon) for me automatically... Could you sort out the auto-filling of a link's details when I add it'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented save flow required manual title/description entry, diverging from REF-BM-02 (auto-collect title/description/favicon/preview on save). Client explicitly supplied the reference-conforming behaviour to replace the mismatch = correct.

decisions.evidence: R1 maker presented only 'favorite bookmarks'; R1 client: 'I'd expected a way to mark a link as "read it later" and then see just those in one place — a to-read pile that empties as I get through it. The star/favorite is nice... but it isn't quite the same as a reading queue... and a read-later view'.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-later/unread (REF-BM-17), separate unread view (REF-BM-18), and mark-read-removes (REF-BM-19) were absent from the presented scope, which offered only favorites. Client identified the difference (favorite != reading queue) and requested the missing related reference requirements = extend.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: 'Pasting a URL now automatically fetches its title, description, and favicon. Fields remain editable, with loading, retry, and manual fallback states.'; R2 client: 'the app went and filled in the title and description on its own — I just pasted and saved.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Revised presentation now conforms to REF-BM-02 and REF-BM-03 (auto-collected fields remain editable). Client response is bare approval; recorded as conforming fulfilment of the same requirement at a later point, not a new divergence.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker: 'Added a dedicated Read later view with a live count... "Mark as read" immediately removes an item from the queue.'; R2 client: 'the "Read later" pile is right there in the sidebar with its count... marking one as read clears it out of the queue.'
decisions.note: Implementation review. Revised presentation now conforms to REF-BM-17/18/19. Client gives bare approval; conforming fulfilment, not a new divergence.
